brief.headline: Push for a 10-15% price cut — they keep 7.4% profit vs 5.0% peer average, and we have four strong packaging alternates ready to quote

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10-15% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.basis: Market research shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume. They keep 7.4% profit on every sale — 2.4 points above similar firms (5.0%) — so there's room in their price. We're at MARKET-FAIR today but can tighten to the lower end of the asking band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to payment on delivery (0 days) in exchange for 3-4% off list price
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹3.29 L of our cash that's currently stuck waiting 30 days; if we go halfway (15 days faster) we free ₹1.64 L

brief.financialLeverage: PGP Glass is financially solid — CARE A+ / Stable rating, ₹3373.51 Cr revenue, and they keep 7.4% profit (well above the 5.0% peer median). Their cash is tied up for 78 days vs 71 for similar firms, so they'd value faster payment. But we're tiny — just ₹39.99 L or 0.01% of their sales — so we have almost no pull on volume alone. The real lever is competition: we have four credible packaging alternates (two listed giants, two large converters) ready to quote, and they know rigid-plastic packaging is a crowded market. Play that card — they can't afford to lose even a small customer to a competitor when margins are this good. Their distress score sits in the grey zone (Altman Z 1.45), and they have EPF payment delays and pending legal cases, so don't push so hard you spook them into supply trouble — frame it as locking in a long-term partnership at a fair price.

evidence.point: They keep 7.4% profit on every ₹100 they sell, vs 5.0% for similar firms — room in the price
Market ask for a 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume
We're only 0.01% of their ₹3373.51 Cr revenue — tiny on our own
Their cash is stuck for 78 days, longer than similar firms at 71 days — they'd value faster payment
They borrow money at about 7.02% (range 3.84-9%) — paying early is worth roughly that rate to them
Strong credit rating CARE A+ / Stable, so little risk they'll fail — we can push harder

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — top second-source candidate already supplying us for other packaging

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, pharma — strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging player with broad capability across bottles and caps

risks: We're 0.01% of their sales (₹39.99 L out of ₹3373.51 Cr) — alone we have almost no pull; bundle more SKUs, commit volume for 2-3 years, or show them competitor quotes to get traction

Distress score in grey zone (Altman Z 1.45), plus EPF payment delays and pending legal cases — don't squeeze so hard you tip a fragile supplier into supply trouble; frame the ask as a partnership lock-in, not a raid

Rigid-plastic packaging is crowded and competitive — if we push too hard without a credible alternate RFQ in hand, they may call our bluff; have at least one alternate (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) priced before the meeting

Market ask shows 'modest headroom' to ₹0.65–0.80 only at higher volume or looser spec — if we can't commit volume or flex spec, the 10-15% cut may not land; know which levers (volume, lead time, spec) we can actually give them
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a long-term partnership on rigid plastic packaging — the market shows room at ₹0.65–0.80 per piece at scale, and we're ready to commit volume and faster payment in exchange for a 10-15% price cut starting this quarter.
